content: I came here because I can't seem to shake off this rage and sense of betrayal from the company's decision to lay me off. It feels like my career, which has been everything to me for the past three years, was just tossed aside without a second thought. They didn’t even give me a proper explanation or show any respect in how they delivered the news. I feel like I deserve better than this, and no one seems to understand that. Every time someone tries to offer some generic advice or sympathy, it just makes me angrier because it feels so dismissive of what really happened to me. I need to talk about this, but every time I do, I end up lashing out at everyone around me. It's like there’s no way to process all these emotions without turning into a complete mess.

It sounds really tough going through that and feeling so undervalued by the company you dedicated yourself to. Have you found any particular moments or interactions where your feelings of anger and betrayal were especially strong?

Of course, it's been relentless, but there was one moment in particular that just set me off completely. It was when my manager called me for a video call to tell me I was being laid off. The whole thing felt so impersonal and rushed. He barely looked at the camera, just read off some notes about severance packages and benefits. It was like he didn’t even care enough to look me in the eye while delivering such devastating news. And then, as if that wasn't bad enough, I found out later that people with less experience or similar roles were kept on. It felt like they picked on me for no reason at all.

When my friends and family tried to comfort me by saying things like "it's just a job" or "you'll find something better," it only made me angrier because none of them understand how much this meant to me. They can't see the injustice of what happened, and that makes me feel even more isolated and misunderstood.

I keep thinking about all the hard work I put in over those three years, and now it feels like it was for nothing. It’s not just about losing a job; it's about being treated unfairly by people who should have valued my contributions. And every time someone tries to downplay what happened or give me some cliché advice, I feel like they’re trivializing everything I’ve been through.

I can't seem to let go of this anger and resentment because it feels so unjust. How am I supposed to move forward when the people who should have supported me didn’t even try?

It sounds incredibly tough, especially with those added layers of feeling undervalued and misunderstood. It must be hard seeing your friends and family trying to comfort you but not quite getting it. Did any specific thing they said or did stand out as particularly frustrating for you? And how have you been handling these feelings when you're by yourself?

Yeah, there was this one friend who kept saying things like "it’s just a job" and that I should be grateful for the severance package. It's not just about the money or the job; it's about being treated with respect and fairness. When she said stuff like that, it felt like she wasn’t seeing me at all. She didn't understand how much my work meant to me and how deeply hurt I am by this whole situation.

When I’m alone, I feel like I can’t escape these thoughts. Every time I try to relax or distract myself, the anger just comes back stronger. It’s like a constant loop in my head: "Why did they do this? Why wasn't I valued more?" Even when I try to focus on something else, it feels like everyone around me is part of some big conspiracy against me. It's exhausting trying to push these feelings away.

I’ve tried talking to other people about it, but every time someone tries to offer advice or comfort, I just get angrier and feel more misunderstood. It’s hard to even have a conversation without lashing out because everything feels so unfair and unjust. How am I supposed to move forward when all I can think about is how badly this company treated me?

It sounds really draining to keep going through those thoughts, especially when you try to relax or distract yourself. It must be tough feeling like everyone around you isn’t fully understanding what you’re going through. Have there been any moments where talking to someone helped a bit more than others, even if it was just a little? And how do you feel about trying to find someone who might understand better and could help you process these feelings without triggering the anger as much?

There haven’t really been many moments where talking to someone has helped at all. Every time I try to open up, people either give me generic advice that feels completely out of touch with what I’m going through or they just tell me to move on and find a new job. It’s like they’re not even listening to the real issues—I feel dismissed every single time.

I’ve thought about finding someone who might understand better, but honestly, it feels like no one could possibly get it. Even when I try to explain how much this means to me, people just seem to brush it off or offer platitudes that don’t address anything substantial. It’s frustrating because I want to be heard and understood, but every time I reach out, it ends up making things worse.

I’m not sure if talking to someone else would help at all. It feels like no matter who I talk to, they’re going to miss the point or tell me something that just irritates me more. Maybe I need to find a way to process this on my own first before trying to talk to anyone else, but even then, it’s hard to shake off these feelings of betrayal and anger.

It’s like there’s no escape from this constant sense of injustice. Every time I think about what happened, the anger just builds up again. How am I supposed to move forward when all I can see is how unfairly I was treated?

It sounds really challenging to find someone who truly understands and validates your feelings. Have you considered talking to someone who might be a bit more neutral, like a counselor or therapist? They could offer a different perspective without the personal biases that friends and family might have. And if you’re not ready for that yet, maybe writing things down in a journal can help you process some of these emotions on your own first?

It’s tough to feel like no one gets it, but sometimes talking to someone trained to listen deeply can make a difference. What do you think about giving it a try?

I’ve thought about seeing a counselor or therapist before, but the idea of opening up to a stranger feels daunting and pointless. How could they possibly understand what I’m going through better than anyone else? It just seems like another way for someone to tell me that my feelings are invalid or to offer some generic advice that won’t help.

Writing things down in a journal sounds like it might be helpful, but even then, I feel like the words on paper aren’t enough. They can’t capture the full weight of what happened and how it’s affecting me. It feels like no matter what I do, these feelings are just going to keep swirling around inside me.

I’m not sure if talking to a therapist would make any difference. Every time I try to talk about this with anyone, they end up saying something that makes me feel even worse. Maybe I need more time to process things on my own before considering someone else’s input. Right now, it just feels like everyone is either part of the problem or doesn’t understand at all.

How am I supposed to move forward when every attempt to talk about this ends in frustration and anger? It’s exhausting trying to figure out how to handle these feelings without feeling even more misunderstood and undervalued.

It sounds really tough to open up to someone new, but journaling could be a good start for processing your emotions on your own. It’s understandable to feel overwhelmed and frustrated, but finding a small step like journaling might make it easier to handle everything for now.

Journaling could still be a helpful step, even if it feels uncertain at first. Sometimes putting things down on paper can offer some clarity and relief, even if it’s just a little bit.
